title: Live TV start outcomes — one truth for the web, Apple and Android lease reducers
notes: Three clients, one reducer. Each answer below is what the server said (or failed to say) to POST /api/v1/live-tv/sessions, and what the client must do with it — the same shape tests/playback/live-tv-guide-cases.json already uses for the grid.

`render` is the copy key the client shows. `offer_retry` is whether the error view offers a retry control. `keep_hint` is whether the persisted {request_id, touched_at} hint survives the answer; `replay` is whether the lease re-sends the POST once with the same request id.

The rule the table encodes: a hint is kept unless the body is typed with owner_decided true, or is a typed 4xx the ingress decided before it ever reached an owner (invalid_request, admin_required, invalid_settings, live_tv_disabled). Anything the owner did not decide leaves a start that may or may not exist, and the hint is the only handle for retiring it.
There is no start_outcome_unknown. An answer that never arrived is `no_answer`: the client says the server did not answer and the next press repeats — it never refuses to start.

`protocols` is the intersection the ingress publishes on GET /api/v1/live-tv/channels. An ingress that omits the field is older than this contract: no request_id on the body, no /live-tv/starts/* routes, hints kept for later.
Timings that pace these flows live in tests/playback/player-input-contract.json under live.timings, and reach the clients through scripts/player-contract-table --embed.
